evidence.curator_note: EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXT: this is the dissociation of the mass-selected even-electron oxonium ion C2H5O+=CH2 (m/z 59), itself generated by EI alpha-cleavage of diethyl ether; not a 70 eV EI reaction of a molecular ion. The 'i' label is a reaction-type mark (i = inductive, rH = H-rearrangement), NOT an electron-pushing arrow (0 arcs drawn). Abundance 'CAD: 9%' is a collision-activated-dissociation branching yield, not an EI intensity. Eq 8.10, upper ('i') branch of the fork drawn from the even-electron oxocarbenium ion C2H5O(+)=CH2 (m/z 59, itself the alpha-cleavage fragment of the diethyl-ether molecular ion). Inductive (charge-migration) cleavage: the C2-O3 sigma bond breaks heterolytically, both electrons going to oxygen, giving the ethyl cation C2H5+ (m/z 29) and neutral formaldehyde O=CH2 (PA = 7.4 eV printed). Book draws 0 electron-pushing arcs; the page shows only the net reaction arrow labelled 'i' (inductive) and the product formulae. The single 2-electron move encoded (C2-O3 bonding pair -> O lone pair) is implied by the reaction type and products, not drawn on the page. The printed '9%' is a CAD (collision-activated dissociation) branching abundance of the mass-selected m/z 59 ion, not a 70 eV EI intensity.

Cross-link: MØD rule IMS_8_10 ('Field Rule 8.10 inductive', src/data_generation/rules/IMS_chap8_examples.py). VERIFIED MATCH. Its LHS [C]1(H3)[C]5(H2)[O+]8{=}[C]9(H2) is exactly this substrate C2H5O(+)=CH2 (rule map C1=my C1 ethyl-CH3, C5=my C2, O8=my O3, C9=my C4). RHS cleaves the C5-O8 bond, puts +1 on C5 and neutralises O8 while keeping the O8=C9 double bond -> C2H5+ + O=CH2, identical bond changes to this record. No new multiple bond forms; cleaved bond is the C-O sigma. Rule fires on this substrate.
